principles: Advisory and read-only: the instrument reports, it never writes, files findings, or touches a gate.
Pure-leaf isolation: validity logic is computation over injected data (fileExists), zero I/O in the leaf.
Determinism preserved: no change to localSignature, signalScore, promptHash, or any gated material.
Honest metric: valid-rate uses an anchored-only denominator and reports unanchored separately so it is not diluted.
Minimal blast radius: reuse existing derivation + store ports; add no new persisted state.
drivers: Must not affect determinism, scoring, or any gate (Experience Layer is advisory by design).
Must be re-runnable on live finding history without persisting anything.
Result must be comparable to Baseline A's finding-level 8% drift number.

options.name: Read-only derive-then-validate CLI
pros: No dependency on a persisted signals cache — always reflects current findings + HEAD.
Zero gate/determinism risk: derives without projectRoot (no write), checks anchors, prints.
Smallest surface: reuses deriveFindingSignalsFromStore and the recall.ts read-only pattern.
cons: Recomputes signals on each run (acceptable: the data set is small and this is an out-of-band instrument).

options.name: Persist validity flags + auto-demote stale signals
pros: Surfaced signals could self-filter stale entries without a separate command.
cons: Introduces a write path and auto-demotion — explicitly out of scope for this story.
Determinism/gate risk if the cache feeds any scored surface.
Premature before forward confirmation-HEAD capture exists.

options.name: Blob-equality unchanged-since-confirmation tier
pros: Stronger validity: detects a file that still exists but was rewritten since the finding was confirmed.
cons: Needs forward capture of the confirmation HEAD on each finding — touches the finding write path.
Cannot be computed from existing data; belongs to the later forward-capture story.

rationale: The read-only derive-then-validate path delivers the valid-rate/drift instrument with zero gate, scoring, or write-path risk, is always current because it recomputes from live findings and HEAD, and is directly comparable to Baseline A. The persisted/auto-demote and blob-equality options add write paths or forward-capture requirements that are explicitly out of this conservative story's scope.

preMortem.scenario: The re-validation leaf stops being pure.
preMortem.trigger: A developer imports fs or child_process (git) into core/experience-revalidation.ts to check files directly instead of using the injected fileExists predicate.
preMortem.consequence: Pure-leaf isolation and hermetic testability break; the leaf becomes environment-dependent and non-deterministic.
preMortem.mitigation: fileExists is an injected parameter; the verifier statically asserts the leaf imports only ./experience-layer-types.js, and the hermetic smoke drives it with a stub predicate (no real fs).

preMortem.scenario: valid-rate is misleadingly low or high.
preMortem.trigger: Signals with no anchorFiles (unanchored) are counted in the denominator, or a partially-stale signal is marked stale.
preMortem.consequence: The drift number is not comparable to Baseline A and over/under-states staleness.
preMortem.mitigation: Denominator is anchored-only with unanchored reported separately; a signal is stale only when ALL anchors are gone; the smoke asserts exact validRate/driftRate on a fixed fixture.

preMortem.scenario: The handler accidentally writes state or touches a gate.
preMortem.trigger: Passing projectRoot to deriveFindingSignalsFromStore (persists the cache) or calling a finding/gate API from the handler.
preMortem.consequence: Violates the read-only contract, pollutes .lattice/learning, or perturbs a gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Derive WITHOUT projectRoot; no finding/gate APIs are imported; the verifier greps the handler for write/finding/gate calls and the story mirrors the recall.ts read-only handler.

preMortem.scenario: git HEAD is unavailable (empty/detached repo or non-git cwd).
preMortem.trigger: `git ls-tree -r --name-only -z HEAD` fails because there is no HEAD.
preMortem.consequence: The command throws instead of degrading.
preMortem.mitigation: Wrap the git call in try/catch returning an empty file set (mirroring currentMaterialHash returning undefined); the report then shows 0 anchored-live and a clear note rather than crashing.
